Card paydown

CP-01 / The day that counts

The balance a bank sees is the one on your card the day the statement closes.

Your own file already shows which card to pay first and the exact balance to bring it to.

  • On this sample screen, the card reports a $1,050 balance, so it reads as 13.1% used.
  • Pay the card off on the due date, and the higher balance has already gone to the bureaus.
  • Your card sends its balance to the bureaus on the day the statement CLOSES. Pay it in full on the due date, and the high balance already went out.
  • Your own file already shows which card to pay first and the exact balance to bring it to, and nobody hands you either one when you open a card.
  • This is a sample Blueprint screen. The card reports a $1,050 balance next to its limit, and the tile under it reads 13.1% used.
  • That reported balance is what a bank READS when you apply. Whatever you paid after the statement closed waits until the next month's report.
  • Two things decide what this part of your file says: which card your money goes to first, and the balance you pay it down to.
  • The system works out both from your own report. Get them right, and the balance a bank sees comes down with the very next statement.

CP-02 / Which card first

Your first dollar goes on the card using the biggest share of its limit.

  • The system ranks every card on your file by how much of its limit is used, highest first.
  • Your credit analysis names that card, how full it is, and the balance to bring it to.
  • The first money you put down goes to the fastest win on your report.
  • Every card on your report gets measured by the SHARE of its limit you're using, and that share is what moves your file.
  • The system ranks your cards from the fullest to the emptiest, and your money goes on them in that exact order, starting at the top.
  • Read the sentence from this sample's credit analysis. It names the card, First Platypus Bank, how full it is, and the balance to bring it down to.
  • The analysis calls that card the fastest win on your whole report, which is exactly why your money starts there.
  • If you've got cash set aside, you enter it, and the paydown tool splits it across your cards in that same ORDER, fullest first.
  • No more guessing which bill to pay down first. Your first dollars land on the fastest win your report has.

CP-03 / What the full card costs

Near 40% used, this sample card failed the engine's card check before a bank ever saw it.

  • This sample card started near 40% used, so the whole file failed that check.
  • The plan goes further than 30%, all the way to 10% of the limit, which is $800 on this sample card.
  • Every application sent before the card comes down gets read at the higher balance.
  • A full card costs you before any bank even looks. The engine checks whether your cards sit at 30% used or LESS.
  • This sample card started near 40% used. That put the whole file past the line, so it failed that check before a single application went out.
  • Every application sent while the card reports that high gets read at that HIGH balance, and the inquiry it leaves stays on the report after.
  • That's why the plan doesn't stop at 30%. It goes all the way to 10% of the limit, which is $800 on this sample card.
  • Read the two bars. At the start, the card sits near 40% used, past the dashed 30% line. At the target, it sits at $800, 10% of its limit.
  • Every card on your file gets that same rule, 10% of its own limit, so each one comes with its own target balance to pay toward.

CP-04 / When to pay

You get a text before each statement date, while your payment still changes what reports.

  • The text comes ahead of the close date, so your payment lands in time to change what reports that month.
  • Pay after the close, and that month's high balance has already gone to the bureaus.
  • Your due date is a different day with a different job, and a separate reminder covers it.
  • The timing is handled for you. The system knows each card's statement date and texts you BEFORE it, while your payment still counts.
  • Walk the strip with me. You pay the card, then the statement closes, and on that day the balance goes to the bureaus. That's the one a bank reads.
  • Pay after the close, and that month's high balance has already gone out. The lower balance waits a whole cycle to show up.
  • Your due date is a DIFFERENT day with a different job. It keeps the account current, and a separate reminder covers that one.
  • A big new charge before the close raises your card use too, and the bank reads that just the same as an old balance.
  • Every payment you make then shows up on the report it was meant for, instead of a month late.

This sample's step, pay First Platypus Bank down to $800, closed itself on a fresh pull.

  • Split it into as many payments as you want, because every dollar moves the balance down toward $800.
  • An AI coach watches the open step, and the Fundhub team steps in when it takes a person.
  • With every card at its target and the file ready, you fund yourself, and the business stops borrowing from your savings to grow.
  • This is the real checklist on the sample file. The step reads pay First Platypus Bank down to $800, and it's marked DONE.
  • You split it into as many payments as you want. Every dollar moves the balance down toward the target, and nothing waits on one big check.
  • You don't even have to report it. When a fresh pull shows the balance at $800, the checklist closes that step on its own.
  • While the step is open, an AI coach watches it and reminds you, and the Fundhub team steps in whenever it takes a person.
  • Now picture every card at its target and the rest of the file ready. You fund yourself, off a file that reports LOW balances on every card.
  • That money pays for the next person you hire, the ads you've been holding back and the bigger jobs, without touching your own savings.

CP-06 / Your strategy call

Which of your cards gets paid first, and down to what balance?

  • Your strategy call answers both on your own report, pulled with a soft pull that leaves your score where it is.
  • You see how much you qualify for based on where you're at right now, and which card is holding the most of it back.
  • You leave with the first card named and the balance to pay it down to.
  • The card to pay first is already on your report today. On your strategy call, you watch the system point to it on YOUR file.
  • A soft pull brings your report onto the screen. Your score stays put, and no bank ever sees that pull.
  • Then your cards go up in order, fullest first, each one with its own target mark at 10% of its limit.
  • You also see how much you qualify for based on where you're at right now, and which card is holding the most of it back.
  • You walk away with the first card picked out and its target balance in hand, so the very next payment you make goes where it counts.
  • This call is for action takers, not shoppers, and your first paydown after it is step one of your plan.
